newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan authorities say coffee quality improving.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan authorities say coffee quality improving.

text.p: Ugandan coffee quality improved in the first quarter of 1996/97 with the so-called defective percentage for the standard grade robusta coffee ranging from 3-7 percent versus 5-10 percent in the same period in 1995/96.
Arabica Drugar coffees were in some cases characterised by poor processing techniques leading to many chips, the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said in a report on Monday.

The average moisture content of coffee allowed for export was maintained at 12.6 percent. UCDA said the cup taste showed improvement in body, acidity and flavour with a marked reduction in overfermentation. Arabica Wugars also improved in quality with enhanced acidity and flavour.

Results of the out-turn and screen distribution tests on samples from Eastern districts in the first quarter indicated a good crop with a rise in Robusta Screen 18 grades at the expense of Screen 12. Screen 18 are the biggest beans and 12 smallest.

Despite improved quality, during pre-shipment inspection, a cumulative total of 491,865 bags was rejected in the quarter due to wetness and a high moisture content. These were dried and re-processed to acceptable moisture levels before shipment.
In a bid to improve the quality, several quality awareness seminars were held between UCDA and coffee dealers in the coffee producing districts which are experiencing their peak crop.

UCDA said local authorities in the coffee producing districts had agreed to help the UCDA curb activities of illegal dealers. It said 18 such dealers from the key growing Eastern region had been ordered to stop processing.
In the first quarter, collaborative research on tracheomycosis continued by a task force of scientists from the UCDA, Coffee Research Centre and agriculture ministry.

The results show that the disease is still widespread in the Western districts of Bundibugyo, Kabarole and Rukungiri where incidence on some smallholder farmers has reached 60-100 percent, the UCDA report said.
In the districts of Mukono, Luwero, Kiboga, Mpigi, Bushenyi, Hoima, Kibaale and Masindi, the disease was confirmed as localised but potentially dangerous at the current level.
The Ugandan government, in a bid to contain the disease, has ordered that all Kiboko robusta processing be restricted to factories located within the district of production.
